header: Date: 2025-07-18 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m | Attendees: Maya Patel, Ethan Chu, Rosa Vega (Redwood) / Lena Ortiz, Samir Khan, Priya Desai, Noah Ryder (Caduceus)
summary: Kickoff to align pilot timeline and milestones. Agreed access gating, primary success criteria (latency, throughput, quality thresholds), benchmark dataset and owners, and dates for midpoint review and exec readout. Noted security requirements (KMS/HSM, audit logs) and initial differentiation vs competitors.
topics: Pilot timeline: kickoff, access, midpoint, exec readout
Success criteria: P95 latency, throughput (requests/sec), response quality/accuracy
Workload sizing: average prompt length, QPS, burst profile
Benchmarks: data set, metrics, pass/fail thresholds
Access & security: VPC, IAM, KMS, audit logs
Roles & owners: who runs benchmarks and who validates results
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, then we'll go through the pilot roadmap. Uh, we have about an hour.
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: Hi, Lena here. Ready.
[00:14] Samir Khan: Samir, platform.
[00:16] Priya Desai: Priya — product.
[00:18] Noah Ryder: Noah — security.
[00:20] Ethan Chu: Ethan from Redwood — I'll drive the perf parts.
[00:23] Maya Patel: Great. High level we want a 6 week pilot: week 0 access kickoff, week 1 baseline microbench, week 2 integrate flows, week 3 midpoint review, week 4 tuning, week 5 run full benchmarks, week 6 exec readout. Thoughts?
[00:43] Lena: That sounds reasonable. Our execs want confidence on latency and cost before committing. If we can show predictable P95 under our burst patterns, that's the main ask.
[00:56] Priya: Also quality — we need to make sure hallucination rate is below our tolerance on the 2 demo flows. We'll share the metric definition.
[01:05] Maya: Perfect. For success criteria let's put specifics: P95 latency < 350ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens), throughput 80 req/s sustained for the two flows, and qualitative accuracy >= 92% on our intent dataset. Are those ballpark?
[01:22] Samir: 350ms P95 is aggressive for gpt-sized models but maybe with Dedicated infra and batching it's doable. What's your current baseline?
[01:31] Lena: Right now our in-house endpoint averages 420ms P95 under sim traffic; cost is high and scaling is manual.
[01:39] Ethan: Ok, so the pilot will compare Redwood Dedicated, Hosted with burst, and a quantized on-prem variant if needed. We'll capture tokens/sec, P50/P95/P99, and cost per 1M tokens.
[01:53] Noah: Security: we need KMS integration or HSM for keys, audit logs forward to our SIEM, and SAML SSO to provision users. Can Redwood meet that for pilot?
[02:03] Rosa Vega: On the security front we've got a checklist; for pilot we can support customer-managed KMS for Private deployment and provide audit log export to an S3 bucket. Will that work?
[02:12] Noah: S3 exports are okay, but we need encryption at rest with our KMS and proof of log immutability for exec review.
[02:22] Maya: We'll add those to the access gating. Samir, for access what's your preferred method — staging VPC peering or short-term VPN?
[02:30] Samir: Prefer VPC peering with restrictive egress, less surprises. We'll create a role for redwood-pilot@redwood.com and provide CIDR.
[02:38] Ethan: Great, we'll need IAM role + IP allowlist; also, sample dataset and example traffic shape (QPS, burst).
[02:46] Priya: We'll send two flows: 'triage assistant' (avg prompt 90 tokens, median response 200 tokens) and 'coding helper' (avg prompt 40 tokens, median response 120 tokens). Peak bursts up to 200 qps for 30s, steady 40 qps.
[03:03] Maya: Noted. For benchmarks, Ethan will run microbench and smoke tests day of access, then full synthetic run in week 5 using your sample dataset. Who from Caduceus will validate the quality metrics?
[03:16] Lena: Priya will do quality checks, and I'll own the operational validation (latency/cost).
[03:22] Ethan: We'll also instrument token accounting so cost per 1M tokens is measured by model variant. Be aware quantization changes latency and quality tradeoffs.
[03:32] Samir: On quantization — can Redwood show per-model quantization profiles and perf deltas? We need something that says, e.g., int8 reduces throughput by X but lowers accuracy by Y.
[03:42] Ethan: Yes — we'll provide a quantization recommendation table and run an int8 vs fp16 comparison as part of the week 5 runs.
[03:50] Noah: Any requirement on data retention? We can't have logs with PII in third-party storage.
[03:56] Rosa: For pilot we can disable full transcript logging; we capture aggregate metrics only. If PII is present we'll redact before transmission. We'll document retention options.
[04:08] Priya: Back to timeline — you mentioned mid-point review at week 3. What's expected deliverable there?
[04:15] Maya: Mid-point will be a 30 minute review of baseline microbench results, integration blockers, and plan for tuning. We'll do a live demo of a sample flow and validate access.
[04:25] Lena: Exec readout is week 6 — presentation with: bench results, cost model, security sign-offs, recommended deployment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).
[04:34] Samir: Who prepares the exec slide deck?
[04:36] Maya: Redwood will draft a starter slide deck; Caduceus will add policy/security slides and final recommendations. We'll co-own the readout.
[04:44] Priya: About metrics — how do you measure hallucination/accuracy automatically?
[04:49] Ethan: We'll run your labeled test set and compute precision/recall style metrics plus a small human spot check. We'll also track regression delta compared to your current model.
[04:58] Lena: For the labeled set — expectation is 1k examples per flow, is that enough?
[05:03] Maya: 1k is fine for a pilot. It's helpful to include edge-case examples.
[05:08] Samir: Networking notes: we will restrict egress to only Redwood IP ranges for the pilot; also want to confirm there is no outbound to other cloud services from the instance.
[05:19] Rosa: We'll provide the IP ranges and document egress restrictions; our Private deployment supports customer VPC with no other outbound routes.
[05:27] Priya: Cost model — can you provide a per-hour and per-1M-token estimate for both Hosted and Dedicated?
[05:33] Ethan: We'll produce a cost spreadsheet — delta for Dedicated reserved throughput vs Hosted on-demand. The pilot will include a cost normalization step so apples-to-apples.
[05:42] Maya: Ok let's capture the gating: access provisioned (Samir), security sign-off (Noah), dataset + success criteria (Priya), bench owner (Ethan), and exec deck draft (Maya).
[05:55] Lena: One more ask: run an availability/failover sim — how graceful is fallback to a smaller model under load?
[06:03] Ethan: Good point — as part of the ticket we'll demonstrate smart routing and fallback policies: e.g., when Dedicated pool saturated, route to a slightly lower-cost variant with known degradation profile. We'll include failure-mode metrics.
[06:17] Maya: Great. Any other blockers?
[06:19] Noah: I need the security checklist today — I'll review and get back ASAP.
[06:23] Maya: We'll send the checklist post-call.
[06:25] Rosa: Also attaching sample audit log format and S3 bucket policy.
[06:29] Priya: When can we plan the access window?
[06:31] Samir: I'll try to provision by 2025-07-22; that gives you time to run initial microbench by 07-24.
[06:36] Maya: Perfect. We'll pencil mid-point 2025-08-08 and exec readout 2025-08-29.
[06:43] Lena: Works for me.
[06:45] Maya: Ok wrapping — I'll send the benchmark template, sample payloads, and slide starter. Ethan will send the perf matrix. Rosa will send security artifacts. Samir will share access details. We'll reconvene for mid-point review. Thanks all.
[06:58] (crosstalk)
[07:00] End of recording.

Notes: transcription contains typical ASR errors (model names sometimes hyphenated, 'K-V cash' voice artifact). References: benchmark spreadsheet (link forthcoming), security checklist (link), sample payloads (link).
notes: Customer will provide two representative flows and labeled test set. Pilot timeline agreed: kickoff (access week), microbenching week, integration, midpoint review (week 3), full run (week 5), exec readout (week 6). Security gating: KMS/HSM, audit logs to S3, no PII in transcripts. Redwood will prepare starter exec deck and cost normalization sheet.
closing_recap: Maya to send artifacts by 2025-07-20; Samir to grant access by 2025-07-22; Midpoint review target 2025-08-08; Exec readout 2025-08-29.
